$comment: Machine-readable mirror of Notion > Content Strategy v2 + fond Design System (July 2026), Section 3. THIS FILE IS A CONTRACT. If it disagrees with Section 3, Section 3 wins. No hex literal may appear anywhere else in this repo.
sourceOfTruth: Notion > Content Strategy v2 + fond Design System (July 2026) Section 3

slateBlack.role: Dark slide backgrounds. Near-black with a cool undertone; never pure #000.

offWhite.role: Light slide backgrounds + primary text on dark. Warm paper tone; never pure #FFF.

fondGreen.role: The brand colour. CTA cards, the word fond, positive/solution states, checkmarks.

steelBlue.role: Secondary accent. Safe/good data states, key terms in reframes, CTA text on dark.

signalRed.role: Loss, waste and cost ONLY. Never decorative.

harvestGold.role: Warm highlight. One emotional word per carousel max, thread elements, caution data states.

display.role: Hooks (slides 1-2) and reframes (slides 7-8). The editorial voice.

numeric.role: Every number, stat, dollar amount, percentage. Numbers are NEVER set in the body font.

grid.referenceNote: margin, type sizes, and every other bare px constant below (here and in src/slide-html.mjs, src/diagrams.mjs, tools/qa.py) are calibrated AT this reference width. The actual render scales them by canvas.w / referenceCanvasWidth, so bumping a canvas size is a one-line change here, not a re-tune.

largeTextPx.note: WCAG large text is 18.66px bold / 24px regular at 96dpi, at the 1080-wide reference. qa.py scales by canvas.w / referenceCanvasWidth before comparing against a measured render.

contrast.chromeNote: Deliberately de-emphasised metadata. Held to the 3:1 graphical bar, and flagged if below.

optical.note: Gate 5 measures what a viewer sees. Gate 1 proves text is contained; these prove the composition is not obviously wrong.
optical.fillNote: WARN, never FAIL. A sparse poster slide is a legitimate choice; this only tells you the frame is under-used so the author can decide.
optical.minChromeTypeNote: The handle, slide counter, micro-label and thread label are a signature, not reading matter - a viewer identifies them without reading them, the way a page number works. They get their own, lower floor. Same category distinction G5.1 already makes when it bounds the composition by content boxes and excludes chrome; applying the CONTENT floor to chrome was the same error in a different place. Calibrated at grid.referenceCanvasWidth like every other px constant here.
optical.fillTargetNote: S2b: stack-list, split-compare and quadrant-card are laid out to reach this share of the content box (rows stretch, numerals and spacing scale, body type stays at or under the body ceiling).
optical.fillFailNote: S2b: minFillRatio is a FAIL on these slides only (slide 2 is re-served alone as the feed's first impression); every other slide stays a WARN.
optical.maxGapShareNote: S2b: when the fill pass opens gaps between a slide's own elements it stops before any one gap exceeds this share of the group, so it can never trip G5.1 (maxDeadBandPct, 0.14) by padding.

rhythm.centroidLevelNote: Oct 2: WARN, not FAIL, pending Adi. At S2b fill (>=70% of the content box) a fill layout has ~0.1 of frame height to travel, so two adjacent fill slides cannot sit 12% apart. The rule failed every approved post (31-36, 49): the gate got stricter, the output did not get worse. Set to FAIL once the threshold or fill target is reconciled.
rhythm.note: S2a / Gate 5 cross-slide. Backgrounds: no run of 3 identical grounds (cta-card counts as its own ground). Centroid: adjacent slides' vertical ink-mass centroids (ink inside the content box, as a share of frame height) must differ by at least this much, so every swipe lands somewhere new.
rhythm.centroidModelNote: Predicted ink centroid (share of frame height, ink inside the content box) per layout and valign, measured over posts 5, 31-36 and 49 rendered with every slide forced to each valign (2026-10-02, fillAim 0.70). Fill layouts (stack-list, timeline, quadrant-card, split-compare) barely move: at the 0.70 fill target the group has only about 0.1 of frame height to travel, so two adjacent fill layouts cannot be 0.12 apart. That is a measured conflict between S2a and S2b, not a model error. The gate reads real pixels; this table only lets the solver plan.

thread.note: S2c: Gate 3.2 compares the thread rail's centroid in slide N's last pixel column with slide N+1's first. Tolerance in output pixels.

gridSafe.note: S2e: Instagram's profile grid shows a 3:4 centre crop of a 4:5 slide. Gate 4 fails if slide 1's hook text or hero number box reaches into the cropped side strips.

ocr.note: S2d: OCR at feed scale is slow, so it runs only when QA_OCR=1 (or qa.py --ocr). Run it at the end of a batch. A skipped OCR is stated in the report, never silent.

neverDo: Stock photography or photorealistic people/kitchens/lifestyle imagery
Pure black or pure white backgrounds
More than 40 words of body copy on a slide
The same visual layout on two consecutive slides
The word PantryPal - the product is fond

normalize.note: S2f: CLOSED table of mechanical typographic substitutions applied at render time to slide strings. Same status as PantryPal->fond: not new copy. Every substitution is logged in measurements.json and the QA report. Additions need Adi. U+2192 is absent from every vendored face, so the renderer draws it as an inline vector mark rather than let a system font substitute silently.
